title: Klarna CEO defends business model as Apple launches rival product
summary: Klarna's CEO defends the company's recession-proof claims against its reported losses and layoffs as Apple enters BNPL.

assertions.quote: it is a model that has a very different strength to the ones and i think that's one why people like apple are now embracing it

verdicts.note: A sweeping 'recession-proof' claim contradicted by the same company's own large reported losses and workforce cuts discussed in this interview.

assertions.quote: you lost 748 million dollars last year you're cutting 10 of your workforce

verdicts.note: Consistent with reported BNPL company financials showing heavy losses tied to aggressive US growth investment alongside workforce reductions.

assertions.quote: we never borrow people cash because we've seen that people when you give people the ability to transfer balances take out cash

verdicts.note: A real structural difference: most BNPL loans are purchase-specific installment loans with no cash-out or balance-transfer option, unlike a credit card line.

assertions.quote: a final you know a massive embracement of what to me is a much healthier form of credit

verdicts.note: Apple and other major platforms adopting BNPL does suggest mainstream acceptance, though that alone says nothing about whether the underlying debt is safer for users.
KC Fed: card networks like Mastercard and Visa, and banks like Citi and JPMorgan Chase, have entered the BNPL market, alongside the original fintech providers.
